scope: Every admitted entity in the 49 world and 31 regional historical map observations. Excludes synthetic fixtures, review-queue labels and quarantined geometry.
methodology: Exact source name plus typed meaning forms a browse entry. Entity IDs and individual observations remain separate. Researched histories match exact aliases within explicitly bounded years; no fuzzy identity merging or lifespan inference.

entries.title: Blue Horde
entries.summary: Blue Horde is represented as a political or administrative association in 1 dated atlas observation (1,400 CE). This classification does not establish independent sovereignty, a uniform government, or effective control throughout the colored area. The color names of the Jochid wings are not consistent across source traditions. Kawaguchi and Nagamine identify late-fourteenth-century ‘Blue Horde’ usage with the eastern or left wing, while other historical conventions reverse the colors. This atlas’s label is retained for traceability, not accepted as a uniquely defined, settled-border nation. Compare the political organization, date and source vocabulary rather than matching color names alone.

entries.title: White Horde
entries.summary: White Horde is represented as a political or administrative association in 3 dated atlas observations (1,400 CE through 1,500 CE). This classification does not establish independent sovereignty, a uniform government, or effective control throughout the colored area. The name ‘White Horde’ has conflicting meanings in historical sources and modern scholarship. Iranica associates it with Orda’s northeastern Jochid realm; Kawaguchi and Nagamine’s study argues that late-fourteenth-century Russian usage could denote the western wing or the whole Jochid ulus. A map label therefore cannot settle identity or an exact boundary. Consult the competing interpretations before comparing this area with the Blue or Golden Horde.
